verdicts.verify_by: read crawl.go:227-232 against BuildPlan's changedFiles population, then BuildPlan(root, ["examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/home/deleted.gno"], 0) and check ChangedFiles for a name no file carries
verdicts.tldr: a delete-only PR gets no per-file source page, only the name of a file gnoweb no longer serves
verdicts.details: BuildPlan records path.Base(f) for every changed path, deletions included, because byDir still resolves the surviving directory (plan.go:220-225). Crawler.wantFile then returns true only for names in that set (crawl.go:227-230), so the set of wanted files and the set of files on disk are disjoint when the PR only removed one. A reviewer opening the preview of such a PR gets the realm render and the source index and not one per-file source page, exactly where they came to see what the deletion left behind. Fix: skip a changed path whose file is absent from the head tree before recording it in changedFiles, and fall back to the gnoweb file budget when a realm's set comes out empty.
verdicts.evidence: judge harness at the head tree: C224 ChangedFiles=map[gno.land/r/gnoland/home:[deleted.gno]] / C224 wantFile(home, home.gno) = false   <- on disk / C224 wantFile(home, deleted.gno) = true   <- gnoweb serves no such page

verdicts.verify_by: grep -n 'plan.Dirs' misc/gnopreview/*.go and read main.go:237-247; confirm no test asserts len(Dirs) == len(Realms) or their pairing
verdicts.tldr: the Realms/Dirs pairing the before/after pass depends on is neither documented nor tested
verdicts.details: main.go:241 and main.go:246 index plan.Dirs by the loop variable of `for i, r := range plan.Realms`, so renderBase stats and loads plan.Dirs[i] as realm r. BuildPlan appends both in one loop (plan.go:271-273) and the invariant holds at this head, measured len(Realms)=26 and len(Dirs)=26 on a gnoweb-plus-ufmt plan. Neither field's doc comment states the pairing and nothing asserts it: grep for Dirs across plan_test.go and crawl_test.go returns nothing. A later filter applied to Realms or Dirs alone would pair a realm with another realm's directory and render the wrong package from the merge base with no error anywhere. Fix: say in Dirs' comment that it is index-aligned with Realms, and assert the pairing in TestBuildPlan.

verdicts.verify_by: read plan.go:250-270 for the order of truncation and seeding; build a Plan with maxRealms=2, three changed realms and a gnoweb change, and count len(plan.Realms) against maxRealms
verdicts.tldr: a gnoweb PR renders past the -max-realms cap, up to four realms over it
verdicts.details: plan.go:256-258 truncates to maxRealms and records Dropped, and only then does plan.go:263-268 append every gnowebSeedRealms entry not already present, past both the cap and the Ignore filter applied at plan.go:241. Measured on the head tree at the default cap of 25 with a gnoweb file plus p/nt/ufmt/v0 changed: len(Realms)=26 while Dropped still reports 6. Each realm over the cap is another gnodev load and another crawl on a job that caps itself for time in the first place. The finder's second claim does not hold and should not be posted: comment.go:69 drops the seeds from the indirect list through isSeed, so the comment's list never runs longer than the cap; it is the render that overruns. Fix: seed before the sort and the cap, so the seeds compete for the same slots and pass the same filters.

verdicts.verify_by: diff the realm sets of the capped and uncapped plans for one changed package: `gnopreview plan -root <head> -changed -` (default cap 25) against the same with `-max-realms 0`
verdicts.tldr: the cap keeps an archived realm and cuts every r/sys realm, decided by name
verdicts.details: sort.SliceStable's comparator carries one key, changedPkgs[realm] (plan.go:253-255), so among the indirectly affected realms the order stays the alphabetical one sortedKeys produced and realms[:maxRealms] keeps the alphabetic head. Reproduced against the head tree rather than through the prebuilt binary, which is not on this PATH: a change to gno.land/p/nt/ufmt/v0 affects 31 realms, the 25 kept start at gno.land/r/archive/boards, and the 6 cut are exactly the system realms. The reviewer of a widely imported package gets archived realms previewed while the system realms are dropped, and the comment tells them how many went and never which. Fix: name the dropped realms in the comment, and give the comparator a second key so an archived prefix sorts last.

verdicts.verify_by: BuildPlan(root, []string{"examples/gno.land/r/does/not/exist/lib.gno"}, 25) returns an empty plan with no Dropped and no error; compare against the same path present in the tree
verdicts.tldr: a PR that removes a realm previews as though it changed nothing
verdicts.details: byDir is built from LoadPkgs over the head tree (plan.go:199-202), so a deleted realm's directory has no entry and its path falls through the `p != nil` guard at plan.go:220 with nothing recorded anywhere. Measured against the head tree: BuildPlan on a path under no existing package returns Empty=true, ChangedRealms=[] and Dropped=0, with no error. A removal-only PR prints `nothing to preview`, and one that removes gno.land/r/x/a while editing gno.land/r/x/b comments on b alone, so the change with the largest blast radius is the one the preview is silent about. Fix: count a changed path under examples/gno.land that resolves to no package and name those removals in the comment.

verdicts.verify_by: for each examples/gno.land/**/gnomod.toml compare the module line against the directory: 145 files, 0 mismatches today. Introduce one mismatch in fakeRepo and BuildPlan drops the dependent.
verdicts.tldr: a package whose module line differs from its directory previews zero realms
verdicts.details: LoadPkgs derives Pkg.Path from the directory (plan.go:138) while dependents() keys the reverse graph by the import strings found in source (plan.go:299-300), so the two only meet as long as module equals directory. Built both shapes in a temp tree: with module = gno.land/p/x/base declared under .../base/v2, a realm importing gno.land/p/x/base gives Realms=[]; with the module line matching the directory the same realm gives Realms=[gno.land/r/x/leaf]. Latent at this head, confirmed independently at 145 gnomod.toml files under examples/gno.land and 0 whose module differs from its directory, and plan_test.go:29 writes the two equal in every fixture, so no test would catch the day it stops holding. Fix: read the module path out of gnomod.toml and key Pkg.Path on it, or assert module == directory once in LoadPkgs.

verdicts.tldr: an ignored realm whose ignore line carries a comment or a tab is loaded and previewed anyway
verdicts.details: modFlags strips every space and compares the whole line against `ignore=true` (plan.go:161-166), so anything after the value defeats it. Re-ran the finder's case and widened it: `ignore = true` reads ignore=true, `ignore = true # quarantined until X` reads ignore=false, `draft = true # not ready` reads draft=false, and a tab-separated `ignore\t=\ttrue` reads ignore=false. Such a realm then passes the !p.Ignore guards at plan.go:220 and plan.go:241 and is handed to gnodev as a dir to load, which is the outcome the flag exists to prevent. Latent: no gnomod.toml under examples/ carries a comment on either line today. Fix: parse with gnovm/pkg/gnomod, whose File already declares Ignore with a toml:"ignore,omitempty" tag at file.go:21.
verdicts.evidence: judge harness: C254 "ignore = true" -> ignore=true / C254 "ignore = true # quarantined until X" -> ignore=false / C254 "draft = true # not ready" -> draft=false / C254 "ignore\t=\ttrue" -> ignore=false. grep for a commented draft/ignore line across examples/: none.

verdicts.verify_by: run render twice into the same -out with a smaller -max-realms the second time, then diff `find _preview -name '*.html'` against the realms in _preview/preview.json
verdicts.tldr: a second local render serves the first run's pages, linked from nothing
verdicts.details: render only os.MkdirAll's cfg.out at main.go:106 and never clears it. Crawler.Write writes what it captured and Index(plan, c) lists only c.pages (comment.go:170), so a rerun after the plan shrinks leaves every page of the earlier plan on disk, served by the snapshot and listed by neither index.html nor preview.json. The README's own local flow at README.md:51-56 renders into _preview and serves that directory, which is exactly the rerun. CI hands each job a fresh checkout, so the cost is a local user reading a snapshot that disagrees with its own index rather than a bad publish. Fix: os.RemoveAll(cfg.out) before the MkdirAll, or refuse a non-empty -out without a flag.
verdicts.evidence: main.go:105-108 is the whole of render's setup: `if err := os.MkdirAll(cfg.out, 0o755); err != nil { return err }`, with no RemoveAll anywhere in the package; c.Write and Index both iterate c.pages only.

verdicts.verify_by: read shots.go:184-190: neither error return calls os.Remove(out), and the size==0 branch proves the file was created
verdicts.tldr: a screenshot that renders to nothing ships a zero-byte PNG inside the published snapshot
verdicts.details: chromeShot returns at shots.go:185 and at shots.go:188 without removing out, and the second of those is reached precisely because os.Stat found the file present at zero bytes. ScreenshotPairs then continues without setting pair.After, so neither preview.json nor comment.md references it, but _shots/ sits under outDir and the whole directory is uploaded as the snapshot artifact and served from the preview site. The cost is a dead file in the published tree and its bytes counted against the publish size cap, not a broken image in the comment. Fix: os.Remove(out) on both error returns in chromeShot.
